subject: Request: Narrow geofencing exclusion & subprocessor deprecation window
messages:
From: Jane Morris <jane.morris@edgepay.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: anya@transitwave.com
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: EdgePay subprocessor deprecation + narrow geofence request

Hi Karthik,

Quick heads-up from EdgePay: due to an upcoming infrastructure consolidation we plan to deprecate a small relay cluster (eu-west-2-relay-3) on 2026-09-04. That relay is used for a subset of EU traffic (primarily BE/NL/IE). We propose two options for affected customers: a hard cutover to our TransitWave partner (which involves an updated subprocessor mapping) or a temporary geofence exclusion for those countries routed to a downstream onshore partner while we complete the consolidation.

We understand this touches your DPA/subprocessor roster. Attached is the official deprecation notice and a short transition runbook. We can provide SOC2 scoping evidence for TransitWave and an attestation letter.

Requesting:
- Confirmation on whether Redwood requires a DPA addendum for TransitWave as a delegated subprocessor, and if so a target turnaround (we typically see 10–15 business days).
- Any immediate objections to a narrow geofence exclusion for BE/NL/IE as a temporary mitigation window (we'd like that window to be 2026-09-04 -> 2026-10-04).
- Any SLA credit / exception process we should initiate if there is customer impact.

Happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Best,
Jane Morris
Head of Partnerships, EdgePay
attachments: edgepay-subproc-deprecation-notice-2026-08-23.pdf (pdf), transitwave-onshore-fallback-runbook.xlsx (xlsx)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: jane.morris@edgepay.com
Date: 2026-08-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgePay subprocessor deprecation + narrow geofence request

Lauren / Kimberly — quick triage.

Summary: EdgePay wants to deprecate eu-west-2-relay-3 on 2026-09-04 and is asking for either (A) to designate TransitWave as delegated subprocessor (which would require DPA addendum + evidence) or (B) a temporary geo-exclusion (BE/NL/IE) routed to an onshore fallback for ~30 days.

Immediate asks for us:
- Legal: do we need a DPA addendum now or can TransitWave be covered under EdgePay's existing DPA (EdgePay claims TransitWave will sign an attestation).
- Security/Compliance: can we accept the attestation + SOC2 snapshot, or do we need on-site evidence and a deeper artifact pull?
- Product/Infra: impact to routing and canary — what is the estimated customer impact if we apply a narrow geofence for 30 days?

Please see attachments from EdgePay (linked in original). I propose: start triage, ask EdgePay for TransitWave's SOC2 envelope + evidence and a line-by-line subprocessor mapping; request a DPA addendum template/DocuSign link if they plan to add TransitWave formally.

Lauren — could you lead the legal redline question?
Kimberly — can you assess routing/rollout impact and whether we can do canary routing to our onshore partner without breaking latency SLOs?

If either of you can respond by EOD Monday (8/24) we can give EdgePay a timeline.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

>

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: jane.morris@edgepay.com
Date: 2026-08-24T08:57:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgePay subprocessor deprecation + narrow geofence request

Karthik / Kimberly / Jane —

Legal read: we need a DPA addendum if TransitWave will process customer content in any persistent way or have the ability to decrypt telemetry. An attestation is necessary but not sufficient for medium/high risk customers. For the narrow geofence window (30 days) we can accept an attestation + SOC2 Type II snapshot for an emergency mitigation, provided EdgePay commits to:

1) Execute a DPA addendum via DocuSign before any persistent routing to TransitWave (we can accept a post-cutover execution in an emergency but it must be signed within 10 business days).
2) Provide a scoped evidence package (SOC report, pen-test summary, IP allowlist, contact points) within 48 hours of cutover.
3) Agree to SLA credit if customer-facing errors exceed 0.5% error rate during the window.

We will not approve any geo-exclusion that routes EU data outside of EU jurisdiction unless TransitWave's evidence is provided and we have an exception logged in our compliance tracker. If EdgePay wants the geofence option, it must be limited to BE/NL/IE and have an automatic rollback condition.

I'll draft a short addendum template and send a DocuSign link to Jane.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: anya@transitwave.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: jane.morris@edgepay.com
Date: 2026-08-25T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: TransitWave attestation + SOC2 snapshot (EDGE-DEP-238)

Hi team —

Thanks for the quick coordination. Attached is a redacted SOC2 Type II snapshot and our attestation (we've also included a short pen-test summary and the IP allowlist for the proposed onshore fallback). TransitWave accepts the proposed 30-day window and will sign EdgePay's DPA addendum template via DocuSign.

A few operational notes:
- Cutover plan: 2026-09-04 02:00–04:00 UTC (rolling cut, 15-minute drain per POP).
- Fallback route: onshore partner "NordicOnPrem" for SE/DK if any route fails (we will not move data outside EU for the fallback).
- We can provide a live readout during the first 24 hours for canary traffic.

Attachments: transitwave-soc2-redacted.pdf (pdf), transitwave-pen-test-summary.txt (txt), transitwave-ip-allowlist.csv (csv).

Let us know if you need additional artifacts prior to 2026-09-04.

Regards,
Anya Petrov
Head of Security, TransitWave

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: jane.morris@edgepay.com, anya@transitwave.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-27T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgePay subprocessor deprecation + narrow geofence request — Redwood decision and conditions

Team / Jane —

Thanks for the artifacts and swift responses. Decision (approved with conditions):

1) We will approve TransitWave as delegated subprocessor for the specific relay cutover on 2026-09-04, limited to traffic from BE/NL/IE, conditional on: signed DPA addendum via DocuSign by 2026-09-14; delivery of the full SOC2 report and pen-test detail to our secure evidence bucket within 48 hours of cutover; and an emergency rollback metric (error rate > 0.5% over 30m) that triggers immediate rollback to EdgePay's onshore fallback.

2) If EdgePay intends to instead implement a pure geofence exclusion (routing those countries to an alternate partner outside the TransitWave flow), Redwood requires documentation that the fallback remains within EU jurisdiction and that no customer data is exported to non-EU zones.

3) We reserve the right to request temporary SLA credits if customer-facing errors linked to the cutover exceed the thresholds in our SLA annex. Please initiate the credit/dispute path if you expect visible customer impact.

Next steps: Jane — please send the DocuSign link for the DPA addendum and confirm TransitWave will execute by 9/14. Anya — please upload the full SOC2 report to the DocShare link in RI-4521 and add the contact for 24/7 escalations. Kimberly — please proceed with a canary plan and advise if we need to open a customer advisory (I suspect low impact but confirm).

I'll record the exception window in our compliance tracker (RI-4521).

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
